page_objective: Show how SIPANEL technical diagrams, façade sections, shop drawings, waterproofing details, drainage visuals, standing seam details, envelope-system transitions, and engineering annotations are displayed, inspected, and interacted with across mobile and desktop experiences.

viewer_philosophy.statement: The Diagram Viewer should make complex industrial envelope engineering visuals readable, interactive, consultant-grade, and trustworthy without overwhelming the user.

primary_goals.description: Show real technical thinking through shop drawings, façade sections, drainage logic, waterproofing systems, standing seam details, and envelope coordination.
Allow users to inspect diagrams progressively instead of exposing dense technical content at once.
Make technical visuals usable for architects, consultants, engineers, contractors, and industrial site teams.
Present sandwich panels, ACP cladding, ZIP roofing systems, façade engineering, and thermal movement systems within a unified technical viewer.

shop_drawing_preview.purpose: Show panel layout, cutting plan, drainage routes, flashing details, façade coordination, and BOM/MTO logic.

waterproofing_detail.purpose: Explain sealing points, overlaps, flashing, foam continuity, leakage prevention, and envelope continuity.

drainage_diagram.purpose: Show gutter logic, slope direction, downspout routing, and water flow control.

installation_sequence.purpose: Show step-by-step execution logic and quality-control checkpoints.

bom_mto_sample.purpose: Show material optimization, quantity control, and procurement accuracy.

acp_facade_section.purpose: Show façade attachment systems, rainscreen buildup, substructure coordination, and ACP panel alignment.

standing_seam_detail.purpose: Show clip systems, thermal expansion strategy, seam locking, and waterproofing coordination.

envelope_transition_detail.purpose: Explain roof-to-façade transitions, waterproofing continuity, thermal breaks, and movement control.

thermal_bridge_diagram.purpose: Visualize insulation continuity, thermal separation, and heat-transfer control.

rainscreen_airflow_diagram.purpose: Show cavity ventilation logic and façade airflow management.

preview_mode.purpose: Provide fast engineering proof without overwhelming users.
rules: Never show full complex CAD content in preview.
Show one technical message per preview.
Do not obstruct critical diagram details.
Use high-resolution asset only after interaction.
Avoid tiny labels in preview mode.
Prioritize façade and standing seam readability.
Support fast engineering inspection in field conditions.
Allow inline preview with modal expansion.
Use side annotation panel when useful.
Allow zoom controls and pan where needed.
Use orange only for critical engineering emphasis.
Reveal additional details in fullscreen mode.
Each annotation must explain risk reduction or performance value.
Support façade and roofing coordination explanation.
Use SVG or high-resolution WebP/AVIF where possible.
Avoid heavy PDF embeds on mobile.
Support both quick review and deep inspection.
Load high-resolution assets only on interaction.
Avoid loading multiple high-resolution diagrams at once.
Optimize façade and standing seam detail rendering.

requirements: Do not rely on color alone for technical meaning.

rules: Mirror directional annotations only when technical meaning requires it.
Allow translated annotation labels to expand.
Preserve façade and roofing terminology consistency.
Place CTA after diagram interaction, not over the diagram.

forbidden_patterns: Full complex diagram shown in small preview
Close button hidden or too small

structure: Correct vs incorrect diagram viewer examples

implementation_notes: The Diagram Viewer is a core SIPANEL proof and trust mechanism.
Mobile fullscreen zoom support is mandatory.
Technical clarity should always be prioritized over decorative presentation.
Diagram interactions should connect to analytics and contextual conversion logic.
Viewer architecture must support sandwich panels, ACP cladding, ZIP roofing systems, façade engineering, and industrial envelope coordination equally.
